entries.description: index scans for any indexes that exist on the table
entries.subject: index scans
entries.object: any indexes that exist on the table

spans.text: Possible Paths for a primitive table relation include plain old sequential scan, plus index scans for any indexes that exist on the table, plus bitmap index scans using one or more indexes.

entries.task_id: one|is|outer
entries.description: One is outer
entries.subject: One

spans.text: One is outer, the other inner.

entries.task_id: outer tuple|to|find each matching inner row
entries.description: outer tuple to find each matching inner row
entries.subject: outer tuple

spans.text: In a nested loop, lookups of values in the inner occur by scanning the inner path once per outer tuple to find each matching inner row.

entries.task_id: both inner|and|outer paths are scanned in-sync
entries.description: both inner and outer paths are scanned in-sync
entries.subject: both inner

spans.text: In a mergejoin, inner and outer rows are ordered, and are accessed in order, so only one scan is required to perform the entire join: both inner and outer paths are scanned in-sync.

entries.task_id: between inner|and|outer in a mergejoin
entries.description: between inner and outer in a mergejoin
entries.subject: between inner

spans.text: (There's not a lot of difference between inner and outer in a mergejoin...) In a hashjoin, the inner is scanned first and all its rows are entered in a hashtable, then the outer is scanned and for each row we lookup the join key in the hashtable.

entries.task_id: a path|for|a join relation is actually a tree structure
entries.description: A Path for a join relation is actually a tree structure
entries.subject: A Path
entries.object: a join relation is actually a tree structure

spans.text: A Path for a join relation is actually a tree structure, with the topmost Path node representing the last-applied join method.
We generate a Path for each feasible join method, and select the cheapest Path.
If we only had two relations in the list, we are done: we just pick the cheapest path for the join RelOptInfo.
